name: terminal-ui

frames.best_why: The only frame with a finished bar, three typed lines and the next bar starting, so most of the sequence shows.

tagline: Mac-style terminal types onboarding lines under glowing purple bars.
summary: A scripted CLI onboarding inside a fake terminal window. Shimmering purple bars spell out scanning and profiling steps with percentages, then status lines type themselves out and further bars and rules follow.
appearance: A dark violet terminal inside window chrome with three traffic-light dots and a zsh path label. Rows of monospace characters glow purple as filled progress bars, each with a small star icon and token count, and dashed rules divide sections.
behaviour: A bar crawls to full while its label and percentage change and a highlight sweeps across the letters, the icon pulsing in step. Status lines then type out character by character behind a blinking caret, and the next divider and bar begin before the sequence stops.
demo_content: Onboarding messages "New Role Detected", "New Team Detected", "New Challenges" and "Let's build something great".
search_phrases: mac terminal window with typed text
use_when: A developer onboarding or wait screen wants a terminal aesthetic while the product pretends to get ready.
avoid_when: Every label, line and timing is hardcoded, and the bar enforces a 520px minimum width that overflows narrow columns.
customise: Only a completion callback, a class name and inline styles are exposed; the phases, labels, icons and timings all live in a hardcoded sequence array.
weight_why: A forty-frame-per-second loop repaints every character cell of each bar while typing timers run.

a11y.note: The scripted text has no live region or role, so screen readers never hear progress or the messages.

issues: Much of the tall panel stays empty for the whole run, so earlier frames look like an idle screen.
polish_why: Distinctive character-cell bars in a convincing terminal frame, but the panel stays mostly dark.
title: Terminal UI
